[Testing] This replaces the suite's default `src/hbase14Test/java` source directory, so the existing HBase 1.4 server-target and ZooKeeper-target tests are silently no longer run. Keep that directory alongside the shared timeout tests, as the 2.0 and 2.4 suites do below.

replies.body:
Addressed in 25111cce2044efb3825f5f39e33d1484bbfbdc0c.

Analysis: `setSrcDirs` replaces the suite's default source directory. Listing both directories keeps the existing HBase 1.4 tests and adds the shared timeout tests.

Upsides: The HBase 1.4 suite continues to test server and ZooKeeper targets while also testing call timeouts.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

[Testing] This only verifies that the call association survives; it would still pass if the unresolved address were incorrectly stored. Assert that the request's peer remains null so this test actually covers the omission rule.

This issue also appears on line 66 of the same file.

replies.body:
Addressed in 31fee37d6dfa80ff4b93b9e4526c90e7c7382ff9.

Analysis: The tests checked only that the call association survived. Explicit null assertions now prove that unresolved and non-Inet socket addresses do not update the request peer.

Upsides: The tests now fail if either ignored address type is stored on the request.

Downsides: No material downside identified.
